Coffee could have anti-aging benefits. Here’s why.

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are a handful of foods and beverages—red wine, eggs, and cooking oils—whose reputations tend to pendulum-swing routinely between “lifesaving” and “death sentence.” I usually hedge my bets by eating these confusing foods in moderation.
  • The one item I have trouble consuming in moderation might be the most contentious of all: coffee.
  • Industry observers note that despite my unwavering devotion to coffee, the jury is still out on whether my daily fix is actually good for my health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are a handful of foods and beverages—red wine, eggs, and cooking oils—whose reputations tend to pendulum-swing routinely between “lifesaving” and “death sentence.” I usually hedge my bets by eating these confusing foods in moderation.

The one item I have trouble consuming in moderation might be the most contentious of all: coffee. I am so hopelessly addicted to the stuff that I usually need at least one cup of coffee before going out to meet a friend for coffee.

Industry observers note that despite my unwavering devotion to coffee, the jury is still out on whether my daily fix is actually good for my health. Throughout my lifetime, coffee has variously been purported to protect my heart, disrupt its rhythm, reduce my risk of cancer, and increase it. All I know is it helps me become a fully conscious person every morning. But could my coffee habit actually reduce wrinkles and help me age more gracefully?

A newly introduced study conducted at Texas A&M suggests that certain compounds in coffee might protect the body against aging and inflammation.

Recent findings suggest that however, according to Dr. Dung Trinh, the chief medical officer at Healthy Brain Clinic in Long Beach, California, it’s probably too soon to pop open the champagne (or brew a celebratory pot) over the potential perks of your coffee habit.

“It’s far too early to treat coffee—or caffeic acid—as an anti-aging intervention,” Trinh tells Popular Science.

Despite its inconsistent status as a health food, coffee has been consistently linked to longer life and a lower likelihood of certain diseases, though it’s not certain why. The Texas A&M study, led by Dr. Stephen Safe, focused on a cellular receptor called NR4A1.

NR4A1 is a protein that regulates how cells respond to stress and damage. The study found that several compounds in coffee, particularly polyphenols—plant compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties—bind to the NR4A1 receptor. One of these polyphenols, caffeic acid, is found in coffee and many other plants and, despite its name, has nothing to do with caffeine. These compounds seem to promote NR4A1’s protective effects, including mitigating cellular damage and slowing the growth of cancer cell line in laboratory models.

In other words, the harder your NR4A1 proteins are working, the better your cells may be at fending off damage. Sign me up!

Industry observers note that after researchers removed NR4A1 from cells in the lab, those benefits stopped, suggesting this receptor may help produce them. So, if coffee really helps NR4A1 do its job, we might just have a new anti-aging drink on our hands.

In a recent development, interestingly, caffeine does not appear to play a key part in this mechanism, Trinh claims. Instead, those benefits seem to come from coffee’s other compounds, like caffeic acid and its fellow polyphenols.

Sources indicate that “What stood out to me was that the story was not really about caffeine,” he indicates. “I also found it interesting that the researchers did more than simply show that these compounds could bind to the receptor—they demonstrated NR4A1-dependent effects in cells. That makes the mechanism more compelling.”.

Translation: The study didn’t just show that coffee compounds attach to NR4A1; it showed that this binding actually seems to activate the protein’s protective effects.

Consistent with this, the study also found that decaf coffee demonstrated similar protective effects on the lab cells, providing further evidence that coffee’s benefits may not have anything to do with caffeine at all.

Recent findings suggest that “One of the interesting messages from this paper is that coffee should not be thought of as simply a delivery system for caffeine,” Trinh claims. “Caffeic acid, chlorogenic acid, ferulic acid, and several other coffee compounds all interacted with NR4A1, while caffeine showed much more variable NR4A1-related activity.”.

So, coffee’s superpower might not come from caffeine at all, at least when it comes to anti-aging benefits.

Before you start guzzling triple lattes in the name of cellular protection, know that “more” does not always mean “better.”.

In a recent development, “We simply cannot infer from this study that more coffee means more NR4A1 benefit,” Trinh says. This is because the researchers studied coffee extracts and purified compounds in a lab setting rather than giving human subjects increasing amounts of coffee and measuring NR4A1 activity. Plus, in human biology, it’s possible to have too much of a good thing, Trinh says.

“At some point, additional coffee can bring unwanted effects from caffeine, including sleep disruption, anxiety, palpitations, or increases in blood pressure in susceptible people,” he states. “Those effects could counteract other health benefits. So, this study should not be interpreted as establishing either an optimal number of cups or a dose-response relationship for this pathway.”.

Trinh adds that as compelling as the study’s findings are, he doesn’t yet believe they justify changing recommendations around coffee consumption.

Earlier studies have linked coffee drinking to living longer and to better outcomes for some age-related conditions, Trinh says. But those studies couldn’t explain why. This one offers “one possible biological explanation,” he says.

Industry observers note that like most early-stage research, Trinh says, this study can’t be applied to humans sipping their morning “cup of ambition.” Much of the work used a specific cancer cell in the lab, along with mouse immune cells, rather than testing regular human coffee drinkers directly. And while the study identified a potentially promising mechanism, it’s not clear how this mechanism will translate to human health outcomes.

Ultimately, Trinh says, no single food or compound is likely to be the deciding factor in how well we age.

For a coffee addict like myself, though, these findings are the best kind of wake-up call. Coffee may or may not turn back the clock, but it does stop me from hitting snooze 15 times.

“The much bigger determinants of healthy aging remain things such as regular physical activity, good sleep, avoiding smoking, controlling blood pressure and metabolic risk, maintaining social and cognitive engagement, and eating an overall nutritious diet,” Trinh states.

“This study is a promising piece of the scientific puzzle, not a prescription for another cup of coffee.”.

Real talk: Deodorant isn't a sexy beauty product, but it's arguably one of the most vital. Imagine plopping down on your exercise bike, pounding the pavement in your favorite running gear, or even just commuting to the office without one. Scary thought, right? Growing up in notoriously humid South Florida, I was always hyper-aware of body odor and well-acquainted with underarm sweat—and I knew that deodorant was the way to keep me dry and stink-free.

Recent findings suggest that I've no doubt that one of the products below will get the job done beautifully for you (so please, scroll!). But here are a few expert pointers if you want to shop for the best deodorant on your own.

In a recent development, "Keeping underarms fresh involves two main goals: controlling sweat and eliminating B.O.," says dermatologist Blair Murphy-Rose, MD. That's where deodorants and antiperspirants come into play. The only problem? People often use the terms interchangeably, but they're actually very different.

Sources indicate that deodorants help mask or neutralize underarm odor caused by sweat mixing with skin bacteria, while antiperspirants use aluminum to reduce underarm sweat by blocking sweat glands, notes Dr. Murphy-Rose. "One potential downside with antiperspirants is that they can dry out surrounding skin, leading to irritation, itching, and rash for those with sensitive skin," adds Alicia Zalka, MD, a dermatologist and associate clinical professor at Yale University School of Medicine.

Controlling sweat and masking bad odors are both important, but you'll have to be honest to decide which is a higher priority for your needs. If you're a heavy sweater and want to stop underarm wetness, opt for antiperspirants. If excess perspiration isn't as substantial of an glitch for you, stick with deodorants. My daily go-to is deodorant, but I swiped both types to share the full scoop on the best women's deodorants and antiperspirants in the game. And the best part? Everything starts at just $9.

You've probably seen a variety of deodorant and antiperspirant formulations, and Dr. Murphy-Rose notes your choice should be based upon personal preference and your unique issues. That remarked, there are some differences between the different types, so here's a quick rundown to think about.

According to recent reports, solids and sticks typically have a waxy consistency, are generally well-tolerated, and usually are the best for sensitive skin. Dragging on the skin is usually the primary source of irritation with these, so "try warming the stick on your skin first before swiping to minimize friction," advises Dr. Murphy-Rose. They also tend to leave behind annoying powdery white streaks on dark clothes and stickiness on the underarm area, adds Dr. Zalka. (All of these featured solids and sticks did not leave behind any residue on my clothes.).

Recent findings suggest that gels are convenient roll-ons and are typically light or clear so naturally, they leave behind less residue than solids. The only downside is that they tend to feel wet on skin—so if you're already dealing with excess perspiration, you may not love that sensation.

Sources indicate that creams feel moisturizing and soothing with application, but are a bit more messy and not as easy to apply. They're totally worth using, especially if you're looking to concentrate the application to a specific area or want full-body coverage (think between skin folds or under your breasts). Creams are typically more hydrating than gels and are a good option for those prone to dryness or irritation, notes Dr. Murphy-Rose.

Industry observers note that spray deodorants are quick to use, lightweight, and typically fast-drying, so they're practical for days you're in a rush. "They feel light and dry rapidly with fewer ingredients," says Dr. Zalka. However, some may contain alcohol, which can be dehydrating or irritating for sensitive skin. Sprays can also be messy because you can't fully control where all of the deodorant particles land.

In general, you'll want to use deodorants made with moisturizing ingredients like humectants like hyaluronic acid or glycerin for hydration and occlusives like shea butter or beeswax to help protect dry, itchy underarms, recommends board-certified dermatologist Hadley King, MD. There are also deodorants made with bentonite clay, powders, or baking soda to help combat moisture. Important to note: "None of these ingredients blocks sweat ducts—they work by absorbing moisture," she says. Dr. Murphy-Rose is also keen on deodorants made with low concentrations of alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs) to minimize underarm discoloration and baking soda.

Industry observers note that that's slightly different from antiperspirants, which use aluminum salts to stop perspiration by creating plugs that block sweat glands, using aluminum, says Dr. Murphy-Rose. She adds that most over-the-counter antiperspirants contain 12 to 25 percent aluminum, while prescription-strength formulas can go up to about 30 percent.

When you’re trying to unwind at the end of a long day, turning on the “massive light” is simply not the move. The glare of a way-too-bright overhead light is not only unflattering but oftentimes overstimulating. It can make your otherwise cozy bedroom feel more like a department-store dressing room, leaving relaxation a little bit harder to come by. The right bedroom lighting, on the other hand, can bring a sense of warmth, atmosphere, and visual interest to the space where you spend some of your most cherished downtime.

In a recent development, the secret lies in layered lighting, which involves a series of soft illumination sources working together in concert: A bedside lamp provides focused task lighting for reading, while wall sconces free up valuable nightstand space and introduce a soft diffused glow. Floor lamps can brighten an otherwise neglected corner, and a beautiful chandelier or pendant light doubles as a bedroom’s focal point, even when the light is switched off.

Dimmable fixtures and warm white light bulbs can be especially transformational in bedrooms that also function as an office or a hangout space. Ahead, we’ve rounded up our favorite bedroom lighting ideas, including sculptural statement pieces, portable table lamps, and wall-mounted fixtures that usher in a sense of calm.

Sources indicate that AS A GROOMING editor, I’m constantly testing products from both emerging brands and classic favorites, which culminates in two major outcomes. First, I’m regularly discovering new and exciting ingredients that I’m allergic to (please patch test—do as I say, not as I do, etc.). But more importantly, I’ve come to be intimately familiar with which brands are consistently putting out the best-feeling and overall most effective products to include in your daily skincare routine.

In recent years, the men’s grooming industry has been exploding, with latest options dropping every week. As a result, there have never been more brands available, and choosing which to try has never been more overwhelming. The shelves are packed with a selection of skincare products which, let’s get real, can feel a little daunting.

The good news is that there are now plenty of options out there for every guy, but cutting through the noise to find what actually works can be a hassle. To ease this decision-making tension when choosing serums, moisturizers, soaps, or other grooming products, these are the best brands for men.

Industry observers note that I love Marlowe products mainly because the brand never overthinks this whole skincare thing. Its products are simple and effective. The creams are smooth and long-lasting without being heavy; the soaps are deeply cleansing with strong lathers, and the deodorants smell great while providing day-long protection.

According to recent reports, the brand heavily features natural ingredients (which I love) and never includes any irritating chemicals like parabens or phthalates (which my sensitive skin hates). Not to mention, many of the products are sustainably packaged, including the soap wrappers, which are made of 100 percent recycled materials. Simply put, when I’m browsing the skincare aisle (or more accurately, Amazon’s skincare page), Marlowe is the most reliable brand I can find time after time.

Product Highlight: The Marlowe No. 102 Body Scrub Soaps get a lot of love thanks to their clean formulas backed by always-moisturizing green tea, shea butter, and olive oil, as well as incredible, cologne-quality scents like santal or oud wood. Not to mention, insanely strong lathers that help these bars last for weeks.

According to recent reports, but if I had to pick one facial moisturizer to wear for the rest of my life, it’d probably be the No. 128 Daily Face Lotion with SPF 50. Not only is it the best SPF moisturizer around, but it’s also one of the most nourishing, hydrating, and non-irritating moisturizers, full stop, SPF or not.

Industry observers note that read More: Marlowe No. 128 Daily Face Lotion Review.

It has been revealed that founded in 1965, Baxter of California is one of the oldest grooming brands on this list. As a result, it has a wide range of skincare solutions, but has really been able to zero in on options for sensitive skin over the years.

The brand’s most notable skincare products are all either fragrance-free, like theOil-Free Moisturizerand Daily Face Wash, or mildly scented so as not to irritate skin, like the Exfoliating Body Wash. And while the latter’s oak moss and cedar scent is certainly subtle, it’s also delightfully woodsy and lasts much longer than its initial intensity would suggest.

Product Highlight: The facial scrub is backed by walnut shell powder, which helps shrink pores and absorb oil, and moisturizing avocado oil to create a gentle, soothing exfoliation. The container is also barely over $20 and lasts forever, as you only need a small dime-sized dose to cover your entire face.

If your skin is prone to dryness, there’s a good chance that you already have some La Roche-Posay in your medicine cabinet. But if you haven’t tried the brand and you often battle flakes, redness, or other issues associated with dry skin, I can say with no hyperbole that I’m about to change your life. La Roche-Posay products heavily feature skin-soothing gems like niacinamide, glycerin, and ceramides, all of which help restore the skin's moisture barrier and promote a healthy microbiome.

Sources indicate that the creams feel as gentle as any I’ve tested, and most are fragrance-free to avoid any unnecessary irritation. Not to mention, the brand has more products officially accepted by the National Eczema Association than I can count (I also hate doing math, but that’s beside the point). You simply won’t find better skincare for dry skin than La Roche-Posay.

Product Highlight: Speaking of the brand’s plethora of National Eczema Association-approved products, the Lipikar AP+M Triple Repair Body Moisturizer is specifically designed to combat dry skin with a formula featuring soothing shea butter and glycerin, ceramide-3 to strengthen and protect the skin’s natural barrier, and niacinamide with its anti-inflammatory properties.I’m prone to dry skin pretty much everywhere (especially during the cooler months), but I lather this stuff on twice a day, and it’s barely an problem anymore. Plus, it absorbs faster than any other body lotion I’ve tried.

Read More: La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 with BEMT Review.

This UK-based skincare brand is heavy on the science and uses its own labs to develop products focused on keeping your skin healthy in the most effective way possible. Built on three pillars—sun protection, vitamin C, and retinol—these products not only help your skin live its best life now, but protect it from signs of aging in the future.

It’s an extensive line with popular favorites like the Crystal Retinal Ceramide Eye Cream, C-Tetra Vitamin C Serum, and the Advanced Night Ceramide Cream to set your skin up for success.

Product Highlight: Of all the best-sellers mentioned, there is none I ride harder for than the Crystal Retinal Ceramide Eye. You may have noticed the retinal in that title, rather than the far more common retinol, but that isn’t a typo. Just like retinol, retinal is a vitamin A derivative with anti-aging and acne-fighting properties. It’s a slightly more potent vitamin A derivative, however, meaning two things.

Sources indicate that one, it’ll clear skin and reward it with additional elasticity even more successfully than retinol options. And two, it’s way easier (and more harmful) to overuse than retinol, so take it slow and easy if you’re newly introduced to the ingredient. Too much product can result in irritation and drying (been there!), which is not fun.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll likely find this French grooming brand in the medicine cabinet of your coolest, most in-the-know friend. It’s a Parisian-born brand that merges the French sensibility of simplicity with modern natural ingredients.

What started with highly effective and pleasant-to-use face products (try the Mattifying Face Moisturizer and Anti-Dark Circle Cleanser) has now expanded to beard products like luxuriously scented beard oils, body lotion, and hair products (even solid shampoo).

But what we really dig about Horace is the brand’s commitment to offering options for various skin types or unique concerns. In fact, Horace’s website even includes a consultation quiz you can take to ensure you’re set up with a curated list of items to address your specific needs.

Product Highlight: As someone who has struggled with easily irritated skin and redness, I ride hard for Horace’s Balanced Skin Set. It features the Purifying Face Cleanser, which delicately cleanses skin while eliminating excess oil, and the Hyaluronic Acid and Panthenol Serum to then provide immediate moisture, leaving skin feeling softer for longer.

The trio is then topped off with the Mattifying Face Moisturizer to hydrate and protect skin. Not to mention, it doesn’t leave any greasy residue behind. This routine has eliminated facial redness time after time for me.

Horace also has some great, surprisingly affordable colognes, the highlight of which is Horace Vintage Vanilla. It’s leathery and cozy, perfect for cooler weather.

What started with a razor designed to minimize ingrown hairs has since exploded into a full-on grooming empire with thoughtful, solution-oriented products to be used from head to toe. The brand was conceived to provide grooming products to men of color, specifically, but these innovative and effective products can be used by all people regardless of skin color or type, like the soothing aloe vera and coconut water infused face and beard wash, or body wash, which is the body wash which we found to be the most moisturizing option available. Best of all, rarely are these products above $15.

Sources indicate that product Highlight: Obviously, Bevel has come a long way from its ingrown hair-fighting origins, but the brand’s exfoliating toner pads are still hard to beat. Thanks to a powerful combination of green tea and 10 percent glycolic acid, they prepare skin for additional products by deeply cleansing and clearing any lingering gunk on the face, while minimizing the risk of ingrown hairs or other blemishes by exfoliating the skin.

Developed by the former president of Kiehl’s, Chris Salgardo, this men’s grooming brand provides innovative and intuitive products that are deceptively simple. The founder developed all the formulas from scratch using natural, non-toxic ingredients, and used his learnings from his years in skincare to create products that don’t just work, but that you actually want to use.

Sources indicate that similar to Horace, Atwater breaks out products by unique needs. However, it’s a bit more streamlined with three simple options: normal/combination, dry, and oily. While the dry and normal options are also stellar, no other brand nails the demands of oily skin better.

Product Highlight: This is led by the Oil Regulator Facial Cleansing Bar and Oil Regulator Facial Moisturizer. The moisturizer is great, as its gel-consistency is both lightweight and non-greasy, so oily folks can use it without fear of residue; however, the cleansing bar is what’s truly special. Most people with oily skin understand the importance of using lightweight, non-greasy moisturizers and creams, but few pinpoint the importance of soap in this journey.

Industry observers note that so many standard soaps and washes strip away skin’s natural oils, causing it to overcompensate and produce more sebum (aka how our skin naturally fights dryness) to restore its moisture balance. Not this bar, though—with hero ingredients like charcoal to target excess oil and sebum, and glycerin to restore the skin’s naturally balanced moisture levels, there are few better options for oily skin.

Bravo Sierra started in 2018 with a simple goal: Create military-grade personal care products that can withstand the most extreme conditions without the use of any harsh ingredients like parabens, sulfates, or silicones.

In just a few years, the high-performance brand was offering upgrades on daily essentials like bar soap, body wash, and deodorant with better ingredients, as well as incredible, elevated scents like orris and santal, and bergamot and musk. Bravo Sierra never forgets its military-inspired roots either, donating over $500,000 to veterans organizations since its inception, according to cofounder Benjamin Bernet.

Recent findings suggest that product Highlight: I’ve written quite a bit about Bravo Sierra’s incredible deodorant and how its unscented option is the best fragrance-free deodorant on the market, but the scented versions are equally great. Whenever I’m going camping or planning a long hike, I turn to Bravo Sierra’s deodorants because they go on clear, contain probiotics to help control bacteria, and truly withstand the elements.

I once competed in a 10k trail run in the rain wearing the bergamot and musk, and you better believe I was the best-smelling dude there post-run, as the scent was still lingering after all that. The brand’s cleansing bar soaps also deserve a shout-out as one of the most multipurpose soaps (formulated for face, hair, and body) while packing the same stellar scent.

Status skincare is a thing, and Aesop pretty much invented it. Using natural ingredients and elevated scents, these products don’t just look good on your bathroom counter; they actually work to cleanse, hydrate, and fortify your skin, hair, and body.

But anyone who has ever used Aesop products knows that, among the slick designs and soothing formulas, the aspect that really stands out is the scents. From the earthy sandalwood blend of the Moroccan Neroli Post-Shave Lotion to the fresh, citrus-scented Bitter Orange Astringent Toner, it’s no wonder the brand sells its own parfum bottles.

Product Highlight: This product selection is wide, so I’d recommend starting with a bundle that features curated product groupings based on skin type and need. But a special shout-out to the Parsley Seed AntiOxidant Intense Serum, which is a perfect do-it-all serum for daily use, and the Coriander Seed Body Cleanser, one of the best-smelling body washes around.

Industry observers note that you probably already know about Harry’s thanks to their hard-to-beat razors and shaving products that revolutionized the cartridge razor game, but if you haven’t explored the brand’s skin, body, and other beard products, you’re missing out. The brand known for inexpensive and easy-to-use shaving solutions now offers an entire range to keep you groomed and fresh from head to toe, including the 2025 Men’s Health Grooming Award-winning black lip balm backed by meadowfoam for lasting moisturization.

Product Highlight: The Exfoliating Face Wash and moisturizing Daily Face Lotion for your mug are a couple of my favorite budget options available. The face wash is especially useful, as it helps minimize any irritation or ingrowns after shaving with the help of hero ingredient, volcanic rock, which works to remove dead skin cells and promote cell turnover.

Sources indicate that being a great skincare brand doesn’t necessarily mean all-encompassing. Not every label offers every product, and this is a good thing. I love a wide selection, but nobody can nail everything, even the greats (further reading: Michael Jordan’s baseball career).

Instead, look for brands that have perfected their corner of the skincare world with key products that are specialized to certain objectives, like Bevel with reducing shave irritation or La Roche-Posay with sensitive-skin-friendly creams. This will result in the highest quality options for every skincare need.

Let’s be honest, for many dudes, this is really the main concern when it comes to buying skincare products. Prices can vary substantially across categories, with one moisturizer costing $20, like Marlowe’s No. 128, and another surpassing $50, like Medik8’s C-Tetra Day Cream. Does this mean Medik8 is $30 better and more effective? Not necessarily, but the pricier you go, typically the more specialized the formulas are. So it really comes down to personal preference, need, and budget.

In a recent development, these are generally the basics. That’s not to say they’re lower-quality, just simpler formulas with more wide-ranging attributes. For example, Marlowe’s No. 121 Facial Cleanser is $14 and is uber effective for all skin types. However, if your skin tends to be especially oily and you want a cleanser with a cologne-quality scent, look to Aesop’s Amazing Face Cleanser for $36, which would find itself in the next cost bracket. Speaking of….

Industry observers note that in this range, you’ll find plenty of specialized formulas and quality scents. To combat fine lines and wrinkles, especially if you also have sensitive or dry skin, the La Roche-Posay Hyalu B5 Hyaluronic Acid Serum is ideal. However, to provide that level of additional elasticity to your skin without aggravating it, you have to spend a bit more, which is why it’s $40.

The same goes for Atwater’s Eye Armor anti-aging eye cream. This $32 tube offers nourishment and hydration to fight puffiness and wrinkles at a level lower-priced eye creams might struggle with.

Still, the products you’ll find in this range aren’t the most expensive available. Instead, they’re more mid-tier when it comes to cost. Think of them like a frisky four- or five-seed team that can absolutely make a run in the NCAA tournament, rather than the favorite ones or twos—those would be your luxury options.

Industry observers note that now we’re in the high-end zone. If you’re looking at one skincare product that’s over $50, it’ll either be in a humongous Costco-type container or offering a level of luxury other products simply cannot.

According to recent reports, there is no shame in surpassing these options if you’re on a budget or have fairly uncomplicated skin with minimal long-term concerns. Just as there is also nothing wrong with indulging for those who are able. You won’t find many night creams more skin-firming or youth-boosting than the Medik8 Advanced Night Ceramide, which is why it’s $78.

According to recent reports, as a grooming editor, I’m constantly putting skincare products to the test and evaluating their feel and efficiency. It is quite literally my job. In fact, I drop a recurring column on the latest and greatest new products in the field, so it’s safe to say that I’m up to date on brands and their skincare offerings.

For this story specifically, I consulted with my fellow Men’s Health editors, including Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan and Style and Reviews Editor Joseph Cheatham, on their overall favorite products and which brands they tend to prioritize when searching for skincare. I also considered top-rated options on e-commerce sites we trust, and cataloged the brands that have consistently ranked high in our other various skincare product roundups.

Latest Update: Low-Calorie Diet and Supervised Exercise May Reverse Early Onset Type 2 Diabetes

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The RESET for Remission trial, presented at the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) Annual Meeting and published in The Lancet Regional Health Americas on October 1, found that more than half of adults with early onset type 2 diabetes entered remission after six months on a low calorie diet and supervised exercise program.
  • Early onset type 2 diabetes is when the condition is diagnosed before age 45.
  • Those with early onset type 2 diabetes may be at a higher risk of complications like long-term damage to the capillaries (microvascular complications), adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and earlier death.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The RESET for Remission trial, presented at the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) Annual Meeting and published in The Lancet Regional Health Americas on October 1, found that more than half of adults with early onset type 2 diabetes entered remission after six months on a low calorie diet and supervised exercise program.

Early onset type 2 diabetes is when the condition is diagnosed before age 45.

Those with early onset type 2 diabetes may be at a higher risk of complications like long-term damage to the capillaries (microvascular complications), adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and earlier death.

Typical treatment for early onset type 2 diabetes is often a combination of lifestyle changes, like diet and exercise, and medications.

However, this latest study suggests that a supervised low calorie diet and exercise program may help some people with early onset type 2 diabetes enter remission.

The RESET for Remission trial included 96 adults from England and Canada who were between the ages of 18 and 45, had early onset type 2 diabetes, obesity, and were not on insulin treatment.

In a recent development, the participants had an average age of 38 and an average body mass index (BMI) of 35.2 kg/m2. They were randomized into a control group that received usual care alone and the intervention group, which ate a low calorie diet and participated in supervised exercise programs.

During the first 12 weeks, participants in the intervention group followed an 800–900-calorie-per-day diet and completed twice-weekly supervised aerobic and resistance exercise sessions, along with one independent exercise session per week.

For weeks 13–24, they transitioned to a weight-maintenance diet and independent exercise.

Both groups were supervised by physicians, and the intervention group was also closely supervised by licensed dietitians.

The low calorie diet consisted of 30% protein, 50% carbohydrate, and 20% fat. Participants were also encouraged to drink at least 2 liters of calorie-free fluids per day and given access to a fiber-based laxative as needed.

Recent findings suggest that in the first two weeks, all meals were replaced with specially formulated nutritional products (Optifast). Then, in weeks 3–12, the participants maintained the same calorie intake but had more flexibility in their food choices.

Industry observers note that this second phase of the diet included one conventional meal per day, with daily intake targets that included protein, fruit, and vegetables. Typically, this meant 60 to 90 grams of protein from all sources combined, one portion of fruit, and two portions of non-starchy vegetables.

It has been revealed that at the end of 24 weeks, 54% of the intervention group entered remission of type 2 diabetes, compared with only 4% in the control group. Researchers defined remission as an HbA1c level below 6.5% without glucose-lowering medication for at least 12 weeks.

According to recent reports, “This study proves what most physicians have advocated for quite some time. Clearly, diet and exercise can work to improve or even resolve diabetes,” David Cutler, MD, board certified family medicine physician at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline.

In a recent development, cutler also added that this study provides a clear example of how difficult it can be to enter diabetes remission with diet and exercise alone. He stated that the small number of participants in the study also makes him wonder if these findings can be applied to all populations.

Another limitation of this study, as Cutler pointed out, was that the strict dietary limits imposed on study participants would be very difficult for the average adult to adhere to.

The study also followed participants for only six months, so it’s unclear how many would remain in remission over the longer term.

“It is worth trying diet and exercise first because they can work to achieve meaningful weight loss and remission of diabetes,” he said.

It may be possible to prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes by:.

The National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) notes that losing 5%–7% of your body weight can help reduce your risk of type 2 diabetes.

Early onset type 2 diabetes is a growing problem worldwide, coinciding with the rise of obesity.

Sources indicate that research from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) projects that the number of people in the United States under age 20 with type 2 diabetes could reach 220,000 by 2060. This is an increase of 700%.

It has been revealed that people diagnosed with type 2 diabetes at a younger age face more decades of living with the condition, along with a higher risk of developing complications earlier in life and reduced life expectancy. These complications can develop as early as midlife and include:.

Speak with a healthcare professional about your risk of type 2 diabetes and changes you might be able to make in order to prevent or delay diagnosis.

#155625. The Courage to Disagree

The Courage to Disagree

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1172 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.
  • Sources indicate that at 23, Mike Soutar was appointed editor of the British teen pop magazine Smash Hits.
  • Soutar was much younger than editors working on other titles; in fact, he was younger than almost everyone on his own team.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.

Sources indicate that at 23, Mike Soutar was appointed editor of the British teen pop magazine Smash Hits. It was an amazing opportunity at such a young age for someone who had left school and started life as a journalist just six years earlier.

Soutar was much younger than editors working on other titles; in fact, he was younger than almost everyone on his own team. Feeling the need to be seen as a strong, decisive leader, he modeled himself on the powerful authority figures he had seen in Hollywood movies.

According to recent reports, his leadership was falling flat, and after a couple of weeks, the organisation’s CEO, Sir Robin Miller, visited him. Sir Robin gave Soutar some advice that has stuck with him to this day: “A great day in the office is when I lose more arguments than I win.".

What initially seemed counterintuitive—how can you assert authority if you are constantly shown to be wrong?—became a central mantra for a career that took Soutar to the pinnacle of the media world.

It has been revealed that encouraging disagreement lies at the heart of Soutar’s definition of a great leader. Why, if disagreement can be so valuable, are we often so reluctant to challenge each other?

Many of us naturally like the easy life. It’s tempting to keep our heads down, get on with our work, and avoid being marked as a troublemaker.

In her research into speaking truth to power, Professor Megan Reitz, leadership expert and author of Speak Out, Listen Up, has explored why people remain silent, even when they have something important to contribute.

Recent findings suggest that reitz told me about a leader who was frustrated that employees weren't speaking up and assumed they needed to become more assertive or articulate. But when she and her colleagues spoke to those employees, one response revealed a rather different problem: "Last time somebody spoke up around here, they disappeared.".

The issue wasn't a lack of courage. It was what people believed might happen if they challenged authority. As Reitz explained, our willingness to express an opinion depends not just on our own confidence, but on how the person listening behaves and how safe they make us feel.

In a recent development, growing awareness of the need for psychological safety has led leaders to tell their teams it’s OK to speak up and challenge. But telling people they have a safe space isn’t enough; you have to demonstrate it. Trust develops through repeated interactions and consistent behaviour.

When Mike Soutar reflected on the advice he took from Sir Robin Miller, he explained how he saw a culture of positive dissent in the workplace evolving.

“It starts with trust so that everybody knows that they can voice their feelings, their doubts, their own opinions.

According to recent reports, from there, it moves into constructive dissent, where ideas are challenged rather than individuals attacked. Then it moves into decision-making, where the leader weighs the arguments and reaches a conclusion.

Finally, you move to accountability, where the leader parcels out the jobs, timelines, and deadlines, with everybody getting behind the decision that's been made.

When I understood this, it transformed my capabilities as a leader because it meant I could take people with me.”.

Building constructive dissent on a foundation of trust creates an environment where people actively seek alternate opinions to create better outcomes, rather than spiraling into a destructive culture of blame and competition.

Disagreement that leads to better decisions ultimately strengthens working relationships, creating a positive cycle that reinforces a safe space for dissent.

The ability to challenge and dissent doesn’t mean you will always get your way, but you should always be heard. That only works when the leader genuinely engages, listens, and is seen to welcome challenge.

Recent findings suggest that soutar later moved into his first managing director role at the London dance radio station Kiss FM, where one of his first moves was to change the station’s playlist policy. He wanted the station to focus on playing only "new" music—nothing more than two years old. To mark the shift, he planned a symbolic bonfire of old records in the station’s car park.

The proposal provoked strong opposition among both staff and listeners, who felt that Soutar was destroying a culture they cared deeply about. People warned him, but he dismissed their criticism.

It has been revealed that “We didn't end up having a bonfire. I’m glad this happened before social media existed, because I think I would have been hounded out of a job.

All around me, I had people telling me in advance, ‘This is a really bad idea’. And I didn't listen to them because I took it personally.”.

Recent findings suggest that knowing that constructive dissent matters is one thing, but welcoming it when your own judgment is being questioned is quite another. A culture of dissent has to be source-agnostic, focusing on the idea itself rather than the person who suggested it.

Professor Reitz, whose research explores speaking truth to power, warns that leaders often underestimate the signals they send when challenged. They may genuinely believe they are approachable, yet their colleagues experience something quite different.

Industry observers note that reitz calls these behaviours "shut-up signals," the often-unintentional gestures and responses that discourage people from speaking openly. She describes how her own "thinking face" can become a frown when she's particularly interested in a conversation. Someone who doesn't know her might interpret that expression as disapproval.

The danger is particularly acute when someone challenges a leader's judgment. As Reitz warns, "If you respond poorly, you can just forget about ever getting difficult feedback again.".

Sources indicate that leaders need to respond to dissent with curiosity rather than judgment. Seek to uncover why someone disagrees and what they might see differently.

We can often react too swiftly, shutting down debate without taking time to reflect. Even if the challenge isn’t ultimately accepted, a good leader will return to the person who flagged an alternative approach, acknowledge their contribution, and explain what they have decided.

Demonstrating that their perspective was considered and valued reinforces trust and encourages them to try again.

Sir Robin Miller made a huge impact on the young Mike Soutar when he stated, “A great day in the office is when I lose more arguments than I win.” He helped Soutar recognise that effective leaders don’t need to win every argument, but that better decisions come when you invite dissent.

Constructive dissent requires challenge on both sides: the courage to challenge and the courage to invite challenge.

When was the last time someone challenged your thinking, and what did your response teach them about whether they should do so again?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even Alaska’s bears are not immune from accidentally making things weird or getting a bit too close. Over the summer, rangers at Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska watched an odd interaction between two unnamed black bears (Ursus americanus) taking part in Anan Creek’s salmon run.

“Sometimes the bears at Anan share the creek… a little too closely,” the rangers write. “One bear is waiting his turn for a prime fishing spot, and the other is so focused on the fish he doesn’t mind his surroundings. Did the 1st bear make it weird by backing up, or did the 2nd bear make it weird by staying there?”.

For this bit of humor, the rangers awarded the unnamed bears with the 2026 You Made it Weird Award.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

The largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in the region. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

It has been revealed that according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their antics.

Sources indicate that most SUVs are lucky to tow a small trailer without breaking a sweat. BYD’s upcoming luxury SUV had a slightly bigger challenge: pulling a nearly 400,000-pound jumbo jet. And somehow, it did it on just two wheels. The video is worth a look.

The Bao 5 made its European debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed (FOS) in July, the first SUV from BYD’s “premium technology-focused” brand, Denza.

As Denza’s first SUV designed specifically for Europe, Stella Li, BYD’s executive vice president, noted the company is “confident that the Bao 5 will be a huge hit,” offering the perfect mix of off-road ability, luxury, and advanced technology.

The SUV uses BYD’s DMO (Dual Mode Off-road) plug-in hybrid powertrain, which BYD stated is the “world’s first off-road-dedicated hybrid architecture/”.

BYD’s off-road PHEV powertrain features three electric motors (one on each axle and a third generator) and a 1.5L turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 536 horsepower (544 PS) and 560 lb-ft (760 Nm) of torque.

BYD boasted that “Those figures – well clear of PHEV rivals’ and comfortably more than conventional diesel SUVs’ – are enough for a 0-100km/h time of just 4.8 seconds.”.

To top it off, BYD added a double wishbone front and rear suspension with its DiSus-P intelligent body system, plus front and rear intelligent electronic differential locks with millisecond-level response to improve traction and performance.

Industry observers note that the Bao 5 is equipped with a 31.8 kWh BYD Blade Battery that delivers a pure-electric WLTP range of up to 56 miles (90 km). And on a full tank and a full charge, the WLTP combined range is 537 miles (835 km).

To prove the new luxury SUV’s capabilities, BYD put it to the ultimate test — towing a Boeing 747 jumbo jet using just two wheels.

While pulling a 180-tonne, or nearly 400,000-pound, jumbo jet on four wheels is impressive in itself, Denza’s engineers wanted to push it further, doing something never tried before to showcase its off-road DMO technology.

Recent findings suggest that the Bao 5 was put to the test at Dunsfold Aerodrome airfield in Surrey, England. It successfully pulled the jumbo jet in each of its three runs: one on four wheels, one on three, and the last on just two wheels.

Combined, the SUV towed the 747 for a total of 1,600 meters, or close to a mile, which BYD remarked is about four laps around a standard-size athletic track.

In a recent development, while a feat like this sounds impressive on paper, keep in mind that planes are designed to roll with as little resistance as possible. Top Gear pulled a 747 with a Touareg a while back. The main thing a pushback rig has is weight so that it can maintain traction. That's why BYD put nearly 10,000 lbs of ballast in the back - so it wouldn't spin its wheels on the tarmac.

It's still interesting, to be sure, especially removing two wheels.

BYD said the Bao 5 was a standard, production-spec Ultimate trim model, and the modifications were minimal.

A towing attachment was added, while the interior passenger seats were removed to make space for the 9,920 lb (4,500 kg) of ballast for the two-wheel pull test. In addition, Denza added small stabilizers to each axle so the vehicle remained balanced on two wheels.

After each run, the vehicle was inspected and confirmed to show no signs of stress on the powertrain, chassis, or tires.

The Bao 5 SUV normally has a towing capacity of over 5,500 lbs (2,500 kg), according to BYD’s Denza brand.

Now it’s time to think about your hair type, advises Foster. In addition to your hair texture, you’ll want to find a shampoo that’s suitable for your dry, chemically treated, damaged, or breakage-prone mane.

Now, if you’re dealing with frizz like I am, it likely means the hair is lacking moisture, states Foster. We’ll benefit from conditioning ingredients like polymers, silicones, oils, and humectants that help smooth the cuticle and improve manageability.

Tech Report: Hackers use old Bitly links to re-direct to offensive content

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media.
  • That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.
  • According to recent reports, link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media. According to the service provider Bitly, its hyperlinks in older tweets from many companies, politicians, and even government accounts are now redirecting to “content unrelated to the original posts.”.

That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.

According to recent reports, link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds. The service typically works by pinning a website’s lengthy, complex URL address to a tidied-up, abbreviated shortcut in a digital registry. This shortened address then redirects anyone who clicks it to their intended online destination.

Well…in theory. Security analysts have tried to warn people about an problem known as “bit rot” for decades. In 2009—about one year after Bitly’s debut—Silicon Valley entrepreneur Joshua Schacter wrote a prescient blog post cautioning against what he felt were potentially serious flaws in the link-shortening “middleman” system. Amid the problems, Schacter cited a “new and potentially unreliable” tool that ties an original hyperlink to the “health of a third party.”.

“The shortener may decide a link is a Terms Of Service violation and delete it. If the shortener accidentally erases a database, forgets to renew its domain, or just disappears, the link will break,” he explained. “If a top-level domain changes its policy on commercial use, the link will break. If the shortener gets hacked, every link becomes a potential phishing attack.”.

In a recent development, it now appears bad actors recently identified countless of these Bitly links previously posted across social media between 2009 and 2014. Although their exact methods aren’t clear, it’s possible they generated their own custom Bitly links using the addresses in the social media posts, then used those to send people to different destinations. Bitly says its links do not automatically expire, but paid users may redirect existing links.

Recent findings suggest that many examples were found among the more than 60,000 posts on X from President Donald Trump’s official account. In one of Trump’s previous posts about his golf course in Scotland, the Bitly link temporarily redirected to Wikipedia’s entry on the Epstein Files. Targets also included corporations like McDonald’s, with one of the fast food giant’s 2011 Bitly URLs suddenly linked to Wikipedia’s page about the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

Not every hijacked post funneled people to upsetting outcomes. Instead of a cybersecurity PSA, the Bitly address in a 2021 post from the FBI briefly linked to a photo of a blubbery seal. Another of Trump’s URLs sent you to the popular video game, Geometry Dash.

In its acknowledgement of the problem on November 15, Bitly reported it had identified and suspended the bad actors’ accounts, and were in the process of “disabling the affected links.”.

“Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the concern and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future,” Bitly wrote at the time.

I’ve wanted a leather sofa for many years, but I could never find a color I liked—a detail just as important to me as the material. I wasn’t interested in the usual black, brown, or cognac options, instead preferring something less traditional but not squarely trendy. And then I discovered Pottery Barn’s Jake Leather Sofa in Vintage Hunter, which hit my sofa sweet spot, exuding a deep confidence that reads as rich, grounded, and classy. Its sophisticated presence anchors my living room without overpowering the space.

If you don’t love the stately green hue as much as I do, that hardly means the Jake isn’t your room’s match. The sofa’s customization options—another major selling point—are robust: In addition to being able to choose from a broad range of leathers and upholstery colors, I could also select the style of the seat and back cushions, adding up to a piece of furniture that feels more personal than an off-the-sales-floor purchase. With its slim arms, low profile, plush cushions, and bronze-finished metal legs, it strikes a balance between streamlined and inviting.

In a recent development, how much does it cost? Are there payment aims available?

The cost of the Jake depends on the size, material, and cushion configuration you choose, falling somewhere between $2,000 and $6,000 for most designs. To save yourself from shopping-cart sticker shock, price out the exact model you want, since the leather grade and sofa width can meaningfully change the total. For instance, my 86-inch-wide, 36-inch-deep model in Vintage Hunter retails for $3,999, but a 70-inch-wide, 36-inch-deep loveseat in a Chocolate Performance fabric costs $3,099, and is sometimes on sale for less.

Sources indicate that what are the upholstery or customization options? Did you choose any?

It has been revealed that there’s little you can’t choose with the Jake. Available in an extensive selection of leather colors and finishes, you can also pick the number of back cushions you’d like (two or three) and style of seat cushion (two separate or a single bench). For my vintage leather sofa in Hunter, I decided on one bench-style seat cushion and three back cushions.

What is the lead time for customization, manufacturing, and delivery?

It took about six weeks for my sofa to arrive at my home after I ordered it, which felt reasonable for a piece with customized upholstery and cushion selections.

What kind of couch or seating arrangement did you have before, and what drew you to your new couch?

According to recent reports, my previous sofa was a smaller turquoise felt sleeper from Mopio that I bought on Amazon; its blue undertones made it feel brighter and more casual. I loved the feel, but dog hair got caught in it easily and was hard to vacuum. This Hunter shade is deeper, moodier, and much closer to the sophisticated design I had envisioned for the room.

Industry observers note that what was the delivery process like? What was the assembly process like? How long did it take, and how many people did it require?

Recent findings suggest that receiving the sofa could not have been easier, thanks to Pottery Barn’s included white-glove delivery service. Two people brought the sofa into my home, placed it where I wanted it, and assembled it on the spot. The entire process took about 10 minutes. For a substantial piece of furniture like this sofa, the luxury delivery experience was a major advantage.

What are the dimensions? How does it fit in your space? Would it be better suited for a certain type of home?

It has been revealed that I chose the 85-inch-wide version, which measures 36 inches deep and 32 inches high, and it fits my apartment almost perfectly. It feels generous enough to function as the room’s main seating option without commandeering the full focus of the room. I would recommend this size for a midsize living area, provided that the access points can accommodate its width. As always, measuring the doorway, elevator, stairwell, and turning radius before you click “buy” is just as crucial as measuring the piece’s final spot.

Sit test: Is it comfortable? Does it feel well-made? Does the couch have a tendency to sag?

Industry observers note that comfort is where the Jake has exceeded my expectations. It feels supportive and substantial, and the cushions have held their shape without developing an obvious sag. In the four to five months I’ve had the Jake, several visitors have already stayed over and shared that they’ve experienced restful nights on this couch.

The only recurring quirk I’ve experienced is that the seat cushion occasionally slides forward a smidge. It is easy to nudge back into place and has never become a serious annoyance. It’s also entirely possible that this funky detail has more to do with my sitting tendencies than the sofa’s construction.

Is the sofa suitable for particular decor styles and if so, which?

Recent findings suggest that the Jake naturally fits with modern and contemporary interiors. Its low, linear profile, narrow arms, and metal legs provide a clean architectural quality, while the Hunter leather adds depth and character. However, with the right design elements in place, the sofa would also look at home in decidedly relaxed spaces, with warm woods, woven textiles, vintage pieces, or more traditional accessories.

Is it durable and practical in a modern home?

Despite its sophisticated appearance, this sofa isn’t your grandfather’s precious showpiece that exists for looking at and not sitting on. Rather, I’ve found it to be durable, practical, and comfortable to actually use daily.

Industry observers note that but that’s just for humans; pets are the bigger consideration here. I have a dog, and a few scratches have already appeared on the leather. My current remediation system is to cover the sofa with a sheet when we are home and remove it before guests arrive. It works, but anyone hoping for completely carefree pet ownership should be realistic about the care needs of a leather sofa before purchasing this polished piece.

In a recent development, the Jake might fare better with children than with a dog, since typical spills are often easy to address quickly, while claw marks are harder to reverse (if possible to do at all). I am planning to try a leather conditioner to soften the appearance of the scratches, though I have not tested it yet. Before applying any product, I would follow Pottery Barn’s care instructions to spot-test it in an inconspicuous area first. Ultimately, the Jake is probably better suited to a pet-free home, or to any owner willing to go whatever lengths necessary to protect and maintain the leather.

Recent findings suggest that do the photos do this product justice? Was there anything you were surprised to see IRL?

The sofa looks remarkably similar in person to how it appears online, including the depth of the Hunter color and the overall proportions. There was no unpleasant reveal on delivery day; the sofa I had spent weeks picturing was essentially the sofa that arrived.

According to recent reports, would the couch be easy to move into another room? Would it be easy to move to another apartment or home by yourself?

While it’s more manageable to move than other full-size leather sofas may be, largely in light of its removable legs and loose cushions, I wouldn’t call the Jake a portable sofa. It’s not modular, but rather comes in a single piece, so moving it to another room or home is certainly not a single-person job. However, assuming the doorways and corners cooperate, rehoming its 85-inch span should be possible, so long as you have help on hand.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A simple swap for salt could spare millions of cardiovascular disease-related deaths, new research suggests.
  • In a study published in Nature Health on November 4, researchers at The George Institute for Global Health modeled the potential impact of 193 countries switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt.
  • They found the switch could prevent nearly 3 million deaths and more than 10 million new cases of heart and kidney disease worldwide each year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap for salt could spare millions of cardiovascular disease-related deaths, new research suggests.

In a study published in Nature Health on November 4, researchers at The George Institute for Global Health modeled the potential impact of 193 countries switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt.

They found the switch could prevent nearly 3 million deaths and more than 10 million new cases of heart and kidney disease worldwide each year.

In the United States, this simple salt swap could prevent nearly 105,000 deaths and about 492,000 latest cases a year, the researchers estimated.

In a recent development, about 130.6 million U.S. adults have cardiovascular disease, according to the American Heart Association (AHA).

Liping Huang, PhD, a senior data analyst in the Food Policy Division at The George Institute for Global Health and co-lead author of the study, told Healthline the team started with current blood pressure levels by sex, age, and country.

The researchers then estimated how replacing all salt with a salt substitute would change people’s sodium and potassium intake, blood pressure, and disease risk, she stated.The team modeled a blend of 75% sodium chloride and 25% potassium chloride. The study estimated these yearly results worldwide:.

The authors wrote that the model relied on data from a few years ago and on many assumptions, and that any large-scale switch would take years.

Potassium-enriched salt replaces some of the sodium chloride in regular table salt with potassium chloride, according to The George Institute.Asked where other salts like kosher salt and sea salt fit in, Huang remarked those salts may contain some trace elements “which has those health halos around them, but essentially they’re still primarily sodium chloride.”Huang noted that potassium-enriched salt tastes “about the same as a regular table salt.” She said it’s possible a small number of people with a sensitive palate could taste a difference.

It has been revealed that huang noted that “it’s really hard for people to cut back their salt intake.”“But the easier way is just to replace part of the sodium chloride in our normal salt with potassium chloride, because increasing potassium intake also helps to reduce blood pressure,” she said.The two minerals play opposite roles in the body, according to Cheng-Han Chen, MD, a board certified interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center in Laguna Hills, CA. Chen wasn’t involved in the study.

“While sodium causes water retention and increased blood pressure, potassium will help the kidneys remove sodium from the body and lower blood pressure,” Chen told Healthline.Huang remarked she worked on an earlier trial of about 21,000 people in 600 rural villages in northern China in 2021.

People who used potassium-enriched salt had a 14% lower risk of stroke, a 13% lower risk of cardiovascular events, and a 12% lower risk of early death than those who used regular salt, according to a 2021 study in The Newly introduced England Journal of Medicine that summarized the trial’s results.

The World Health Organization (WHO) endorsed potassium-enriched salt in a 2025 guideline, saying it can reduce blood pressure and the risk of cardiovascular disease.

Industry observers note that the AHA said potassium-based salt substitutes can help lower blood pressure in some adults. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued labeling guidance in 2020 allowing an alternate name for potassium chloride on ingredient labels to include the word “salt.”“We think that blood pressure begins to improve as soon as 1 week after cutting back on sodium intake. The full benefit typically takes up to 4 weeks,” Chen said.

According to recent reports, “We generally recommend a daily sodium limit of 2,300 milligrams (mg), ideally under 1,500 mg a day. Most people consume over 3,000 mg of sodium a day, well above the recommended limit,” Chen noted.The WHO recommends less than 2,000 mg of sodium per day and suggests at least 3,510 mg of potassium a day.In the United States, more than 70% of salt intake comes from processed and restaurant foods, according to the AHA.

Industry observers note that huang remarked that some people with advanced chronic kidney disease should avoid potassium-enriched salt.When the kidneys don’t work well, the body may not clear extra potassium efficiently, she said. That can lead to hyperkalemia, or high potassium levels in the blood, which can raise the risk of cardiac arrest, Huang said.Among people with stage 3 to stage 5 kidney disease, switching to salt substitutes could prevent about 750,000 deaths a year by lowering blood pressure and cause about 100,000 deaths a year from hyperkalemia, the researchers estimated.The AHA said that people with kidney disease or who take medications that affect potassium should check with a healthcare professional before using these products.

An estimated 37 million U.S. adults have chronic kidney disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Potassium-enriched salt is available at supermarkets in the U.S. Many major U.S. grocery chains, including Kroger, Walmart, and Publix, carry two types of products, according to their websites:.

Potassium-enriched salt typically costs about twice as much as regular salt, according to the study.Huang said she hoped people would see the results and start thinking of the switch as “a simple thing I can do for their own health.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As no-drip, low-noise job sites become more the global rule rather than the exception, Volvo’s incredibly versatile EWR150 Electric wheeled excavators are proving to be a smart addition to construction and municipal fleets – that’s proving true in Luxembourg, as well.

The Volvo EWR150 Electric wheeled excavator is helping the postage stamp nation of Luxembourg connect natural freshwater springs to a planned water reservoir, but the work has to be done in an existing groundwater protection zone, where even the smallest fuel spills or oil leaks could have serious consequences. An ideal opportunity, in other words, for a battery electric machine like the EWR150 Electric to shine.

“Sometimes I miss the sound of the engine,” states Thomas Weber, an operator on the project who’d previously worked with the conventional EWR150 wheeled excavator. “But the quieter operation of the EWR150 Electric is more beneficial for me, personally. Compared to the diesel equivalent, I find the performance and power to be identical.”.

Volvo CE took to LinkedIn to share the work being done by the Luxemburgers at construction firm Elenz, touting the Volvo’s clean, quiet running in this highly environment.

Sources indicate that for their part, Elenz executives are equally excited about the latest machine. “Going electric is not a regulation, but a requirement for this particular job,” explains Christoph Schommer, Managing Director of Elenz. “We are thoroughly impressed by the EWR150 Electric. Its low noise level is a major advantage here. At the same time, the machine offers plenty of power and consistently delivers the same level of energy.”.

The EWR150 Electric is built around a 270 kWh, 600V li-ion battery pack powering an electric drive motor that’s backed by a KERS-style hydraulic boom energy-recovery system that works like regenerative braking to extend the machine’s operating time. A 0.67 m³ (~0.9 yd³) bucket with 108.5-kN (~ 24,390 lb.) breakout force is standard, and offers a, 8.95 meter (~29 foot) maximum digging reach and 5.23 meter (~17 foot) digging depth. Volvo says the machine can typically operate for 8–10 hours depending on the application.

Elenz is charging their EWR150 Electric overnight using a 32A L2 connection at a nearby sewage treatment plant, which also serves as the project office and a secure parking location for site equipment. By charging overnight, when Elenz’ crew isn’t working, the organization has been able to integrate the significant BEV without changing their existing work schedules.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that around the world, the number of uncontacted Indigenous tribes continues to dwindle. Indigenous rights advocates estimate that half of the nearly 200 communities still existing in comparative isolation could disappear within a decade, without proper safeguards against climate change, land loss, fame-seeking opportunists, and illegal industrial encroachments. Unfortunately, the situation has apparently grown so dire that some Indigenous groups are reaching out for help—and exposing themselves to potentially deadly foreign diseases in the process.

On November 17, the nonprofit advocacy group Survival International reported a recent incident in which 20 members of the Awá people intentionally contacted local government officials in the Brazilian Amazon. Although proficient hunter-gatherers, the group requested yams before taking them back into the rainforest.

“This is a troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger,” Survival International director Caroline Pearce remarked in a statement.

Sources indicate that the Awá are one of the world’s last uncontacted Indigenous tribes, whose ties to the Brazilian rainforest stretch back centuries. They faced their first attacks from European settlers during the 1800s, which eventually forced them to adopt a nomadic lifestyle to avoid future encounters. Brazil finally supplied the Awá with settlement areas during the mid-1980s, but it still took years before the government properly invested in demarcated land. In the meantime, numerous deadly interactions with loggers, farmers, and other illegal intruders had reduced the Awá community to barely 300 people. Of those, advocates estimate only about one-third of the hunter-gatherers remain completely isolated from the outside world.

“The Brazilian government must commit the resources necessary to protect [the region of] Arariboia from the loggers and ranchers who are razing it, in flagrant defiance of the law,” Pearce added.

In addition to the advocacy work by Survival International, the Awá are supported by a team of Indigenous members of the Guajajara community known as the Forest Guardians. These volunteers have spent years pushing back against illegal cattle ranchers and loggers attempting to claim land in Arariboia, often dying as a result of their efforts.

In a recent development, “The Forest Guardians have always worked to protect the Awá against encroachment, even at the cost of losing warriors in battle,” the organization noted. “We demand immediate action from the relevant authorities…to ensure what the Awá believe is best for them, safeguarding their lives, health, safety and dignity. FOR THE AWÁ, FOR THE TENETEHAR [language], AND FOR THE FOREST!”.

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Michelle Quirk.

In a recent development, at any given time, millions of American adults (and some younger) are on a diet. That means they are watching their weight. Or trying to. Some diets actually incorporate “cheat days” or “cheat meals.” Some people on diets institute their own cheats—as in, “I’ll just splurge on this tonight, and get back to my diet tomorrow.”.

Unfortunately, food cheating can lead to weight gain, failure to lose weight, and diet-disease consequences.

Sources indicate that where does this come from? Is cheating a “thing” in its own right or does it have more to do with food cravings, impulse control, metabolism, brain function, gut health, and any number of other body and brain processes?

Recent findings suggest that to take a closer look at this, we can check out research on people reporting their food intake. After all, that is the only way we can find out what people are eating. Or think they are eating.

How is this tracked? There are a variety of ways, including self-report questionnaires, 24-hour recall forms, recording food intake in the moment on an app, taking pictures of food being eaten, and wearing cameras throughout the day. There are some problems with all of these methods. For example, people may report differently when they are part of a study that watches what they eat. Still, there have been some discoveries that are fairly consistent.

In a recent development, people are not great at reporting what they eat. They typically underreport snack foods, readily available foods, and foods that are high-calorie and feel more rewarding than vegetables. Most commonly, people tend to forget the snacks they grab between meals. Interestingly, people also tend to overreport their intake of healthy foods, like proteins or vegetables.

Digging deeper, there are some nuances.

Social pressure can work both ways. If someone has revealed to their family and friends that they are on a diet or following a certain proposal, they may feel pressure to eat only healthy items when in that group. On the other hand, some may just go along with a group if they are enjoying some party foods. Being observed versus not being observed may also be part of the mix.

Distraction can cause people to grab a food and forget about it.

Negative affect can be associated with emotional eating and giving in to the impulse to seek highly palatable foods, and then have it slip from their memories.

Memory and judgment concerns: One study (2020) discovered that negative affect is associated with decreased memory suppression in the hippocampus of palatable food cues. In other words, palatable food cues become more salient and can lead to wanting those items.

Another study (2019) noted that the Western diet, which includes processed foods, can impact the hippocampus and several other areas to impair judgment.

According to recent reports, the hippocampus is a center of memory and can be implicated in confirmation bias. An article in the Washington Post (2022) noted that “one of the biggest problems to correcting information is the fact that hearing the truth doesn’t delete a falsehood from our memory.” Our brains store the original piece of misinformation, and it takes a different tagging system to get at the truth. To put it in the context of cheating with food, perhaps the eating was unconscious, or perhaps the person just doesn’t want to identify as a person who sneaks food. Either way, there is the memory that the cheat didn’t happen. The memory can become part of an identity or even a system of belief.

Metabolism: Excess weight can affect leptin signaling, so that hunger signals are inhibited, leading to food consumption unrelated to hunger signals.

Sources indicate that excess weight can lead to diabetes and insulin resistance. A study (2019) indicated insulin resistance to be associated with deficits in episodic memory.

Sources indicate that one study (2023) used a trial of supervised machine learning, which did, in the end, mitigate food underreporting. Unfortunately, this is not a sustainable process, or one that could be used widely.

Another study (2015) used Inhibitory Control Training with some success. However, the gains they made were only short-term.

A study (2016) noted that accurate monitoring is “synonymous with the most weight loss.” However, studies that provide opportunity to do so are necessarily time-limited. The process needs to nurture long-term skills to maintain success.

Sources indicate that irregular eating patterns have been associated with cheating. So, one strategy would be to encourage people to eat regular meals and double down on planning.

Industry observers note that another strategy includes education or coaching. Awareness of the potential areas where pitfalls can happen and presenting other options may give people a strategy they can use long-term.

Education could include some of the reasons why cheating is so prevalent. It’s not a moral failure. It’s human nature, and it’s the way our bodies work. Knowledge can start to make some inroads.

Monitoring is a good tool. It is an external process that can lead to awareness. However, the strategies above point to an overarching process that is internal—changing attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors. These are changes that can be realized over time and can be lasting.

💡 Key Takeaways
